title: Round the pack, keep the remainder
hook: Three items per guest, ten per pack: how much extra appears?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Round purchases to whole packs and compute excess quantity.

misconception: Buying whole packs provides exactly the required quantity.
objective: Round purchases to whole packs and compute excess quantity.

claims.text: Each guest receives three items. Packs contain ten items and cannot be split at purchase. Scaled model; quantity-only model; indivisible ten-packs.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Guests=7, A=30items and B=21items. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",10,["ceil",["/",["*",3,"x"],10]]]; B=["*",3,"x"]; x denotes Guests. At x=7, A=30, B=21; recall at x=10: B=30. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: First compute the exact requirement, then divide by pack size and round up. Purchased quantity is a multiple of ten. The gap is an explicit remainder rather than a change in portions.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",10,["ceil",["/",["*",3,"x"],10]]]; B=["*",3,"x"]; x denotes Guests. At x=7, A=30, B=21; recall at x=10: B=30. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Each guest receives three items. Packs contain ten items and cannot be split at purchase. Change only Guests to 10. What is B (Required) now? Correct: 30items. The gap is an explicit remainder rather than a change in portions.

recall.question: Each guest receives three items. Packs contain ten items and cannot be split at purchase. Change only Guests to 10. What is B (Required) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Guests=10: it gives 30items. First compute the exact requirement, then divide by pack size and round up. Purchased quantity is a multiple of ten. The gap is an explicit remainder rather than a change in portions.
